```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use `hte_task()` and `fit_cate()` to estimate conditional average treatment
effects. Choose the covariates to adjust for with `confounders` and the
covariates to condition the effect on with `modifiers`.

```{r}
library(hte3)
library(sl3)

data <- hte3_example_data(n = 150, seed = 2)

task <- hte_task(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y",
  propensity_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  outcome_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  mean_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

dr_model <- fit_cate(
  task,
  method = "dr",
  base_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_validate = FALSE
)

head(predict(dr_model, data))
summary(dr_model)
```

## Choose a method

`fit_cate()` supports `method = c("dr", "r", "t", "ep")`.

- `method = "dr"` is the default for binary or categorical treatments. It
  uses estimated treatment probabilities and outcome regressions to construct
  a doubly robust pseudo-outcome, then regresses it on the modifiers.
- `method = "r"` regresses outcome residuals on treatment residuals and
  also supports continuous treatments. When the modifiers are a subset of the
  adjustment covariates, it targets an
  overlap-weighted projection rather than the unweighted
  `E[Y(1) - Y(0) | V]`.
- `method = "t"` fits outcome models by treatment arm, takes their difference,
  and regresses that difference on the modifiers.
- `method = "ep"` updates the initial outcome estimates using a sieve basis
  before fitting the effect regression. See [EP-learner](ep-learner.html)
  for basis-size selection and the differences between EP-DR and EP-R.

## Conditioning on fewer covariates

When `modifiers = V` and `confounders = W` with `V` a strict subset of `W`,
the target of interest is `E[Y(1) - Y(0) | V] = E[tau(W) | V]`.

In the supported binary/categorical-treatment setting:

- DR, EP-DR, and the default two-stage T-learner estimate this target
- the current R-learner instead targets an overlap-weighted projection onto
  functions of `V`

EP-R generally also targets an overlap-weighted projection in this setting.
Both R and EP-R issue a warning when the modifiers are a strict subset of the
adjustment covariates.

## Compare methods

Set `cross_validate = TRUE` to compare methods and use `cv_control` to set
the number of validation folds.

```{r, warning = FALSE}
cv_model <- fit_cate(
  task,
  method = c("dr", "r", "ep"),
  base_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_validate = TRUE,
  cv_control = list(V = 2)
)

cv_model
head(predict(cv_model, data))
```

`summary(cv_model)` reports the selected learner. If the selected learner is
an EP candidate, the summary also reports its targeting style, basis size,
and the grid of basis sizes compared.

## Treatment types and tuning

- Continuous-treatment CATE currently supports `method = "r"` only, using the
  partially linear effect model `A * tau(X)`.
- Use `sieve_num_basis` when you want one fixed EP basis size and
  `sieve_basis_grid` to compare EP basis sizes by cross-validation.
- For direct control over candidate learner objects, see
  [Using sl3 directly](advanced-sl3.html).
